text:
Christopher Columbus, the visionary who revolutionized the global economy by introducing the world to the concept of "New World, Same Old Problems."

It is truly inspiring to see the explorer's commitment to 'discovery' by repackaging the same planet with a new name and increasing the historical baggage. One must admire the audacity and sheer creativity involved in convincing Europe that what they really needed was essentially the same landmass they already had, but with a sleek adjective added to its name.

While others were busy with the tedious details of geography and indigenous cultures, Columbus had the brilliant idea to simply rename the destination "America" (after a guy who didn't even get there first) and charge a premium for the privilege of being the first to ruin it. His innovation? Realizing that if you call it "New," people will pay extra for it, even if it’s just the old world with a different coat of paint. A true pioneer of corporate rebranding, proving that history is just a story told by the person who showed up with the biggest ship and the loudest megaphone.
